text.arabic_uthmani: أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَخَّرَ لَكُم مَّا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَٱلْفُلْكَ تَجْرِى فِى ٱلْبَحْرِ بِأَمْرِهِۦ وَيُمْسِكُ ٱلسَّمَآءَ أَن تَقَعَ عَلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِۦٓ ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِٱلنَّاسِ لَرَءُوفٌۭ رَّحِيمٌۭ

words.gloss_range: rhetorical negative question opening an appeal to visible recognition
words.prose: {{ar:أَلَمْ}} ({{tr:a-lam}}) fuses the interrogative opening with jussive negation, so the ayah begins as a recognition question rather than as neutral report. That question-frame launches the catalogue of earth, sea, sky, and compassion as evidence the addressee is expected to acknowledge.

topics.headline: rhetorical seeing frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the cosmic catalogue is framed as something already available for recognition, not introduced as detached information.
topics.reason: The compound particle governs the following jussive seeing verb and opens the ayah as a rhetorical question expecting assent.

topics.headline: fused question-negation form
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the question and negation arriving as one compact surface unit before the act of seeing appears.
topics.reason: The surface combines interrogative hamza and jussive negation into one word-form.

words.gloss_range: apocopated seeing addressed to a singular hearer, with recognition and judgment shades locally present
words.root_gloss_range: seeing, perceiving, judging, opining, and visionary perception; local syntax selects recognition through seeing
words.prose: {{ar:تَرَ}} ({{tr:tara}}) is shortened by the jussive frame, making the appeal clipped and direct. The root range lets seeing carry recognition and judgment, while the repeated formula links this ayah with other sign-appeals, including 22:63 and 31:20.

topics.headline: apocopated seeing form
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the address sharpened by a visibly shortened verb inside the question frame.
topics.reason: The preceding jussive particle licenses the apocopated second-person singular imperfect.

topics.headline: seeing as recognition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the requested seeing is not bare eyesight; it presses toward recognition and judgment.
topics.reason: The broad root range is real, but local grammar selects the recognition sense inside a rhetorical sign formula rather than dream-vision.

topics.headline: repeated sign appeal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices this opening as part of a Quranic sign-recognition formula also used nearby and elsewhere.
topics.reason: The supplied rows cite the same formula in 22:63, 22:65, and 31:20.

words.gloss_range: assertive complementizer turning the seen content into a governed proposition
words.prose: {{ar:أَنَّ}} ({{tr:anna}}) makes the content of the seeing claim explicit and assertive. The question does not ask whether there is a sign in general; it directs the addressee to recognize the proposition that God has subjected, enabled, restrained, and shown compassion.

topics.headline: assertive seen-content clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the object of seeing is a full asserted proposition, not a loose visual scene.
topics.reason: The particle introduces the content complement governed by the seeing verb.

words.gloss_range: proper divine name as the accusative subject of the asserted content clause
words.root_gloss_range: divine-name field with debated derivational associations of deity, worship, and longing; local form is the proper name
words.prose: The first {{ar:ٱللَّهَ}} ({{tr:allāha}}) stands as the named subject inside the asserted content clause. Its proper-name definiteness keeps the following acts tied to a uniquely specified divine agent, carrying the sovereignty frame from 22:64 into concrete enacted signs.

topics.headline: subject of asserted acts
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the catalogue begins with God as the grammatical subject of the asserted acts.
topics.reason: The proper name is accusative as the subject of the complement introduced by the preceding particle.

topics.headline: proper-name specificity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the acts are assigned to the uniquely named God, while derivational debates remain background rather than replacing the proper-name force.
topics.reason: The local surface is the proper divine name; derivational disputes can color lexical review but do not create a common-noun reading here.

topics.headline: sovereignty carried into examples
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the move from the ownership claim in 22:64 into enacted control over earth, sea, sky, and mercy.
topics.reason: The contextual rows connect this divine-name placement with the preceding sovereignty frame and with another local sacrificial-use context at 22:36.

words.gloss_range: completed Form II subjection or harnessing for human benefit, not mockery
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes mockery and subjugation; Form II here selects causative subjection
words.prose: {{ar:سَخَّرَ}} ({{tr:sakhkhara}}) presents subjection as an accomplished divine act. The Form II shape selects causative harnessing, excluding the mockery branch, and it sets the earth and ship material inside a wider sign-pattern where the need-free divine subject makes creation serviceable for others.

topics.headline: completed subjection
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the serviceability of creation is presented as already accomplished before the details are listed.
topics.reason: The perfect Form II verb heads the first divine-act clause.

topics.headline: harnessing not mockery
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same root family can carry mockery elsewhere, but this form and context make causative subjection the active sense.
topics.reason: The Form II verb and its objects license harnessing or making serviceable, while the Form I mockery branch is not local.

topics.headline: serviceable creation pattern
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that divine needlessness is expressed through creation being subjected for others, as in the related pattern at 31:20 and 45:13.
topics.reason: The rows connect the verb with recurring earth, sea, motion, and command patterns and with the boundary movement from divine sufficiency to human benefit.

words.gloss_range: benefactive prepositional phrase addressed to the plural audience, with possession as secondary shade
words.prose: {{ar:لَكُمْ}} ({{tr:lakum}}) inserts the audience into the subjection clause before the objects are named. The phrase marks advantage and possible possession-shade, so the catalogue is not merely cosmic scale; it is creation made available for the addressees.

topics.headline: plural beneficiary inserted early
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the audience placed inside the act of subjection before the earth and ship objects are named.
topics.reason: The lām with second-person plural suffix functions as a dative of advantage interrupting the verb-object sequence.

words.gloss_range: relative pronoun opening an expansive object set, not negation here
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) opens the object of subjection as whatever is in the earth. Its value is expansive, while local syntax rules out reading it as negation or an infinitival particle.

topics.headline: open-ended subjected set
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first object field is deliberately broad: whatever lies within the earth-domain is swept into the act of subjection.
topics.reason: The word functions as the relative object of the verb; the following prepositional phrase specifies its domain.

words.gloss_range: locative containment marker defining the earth as the domain of the subjected set
words.prose: {{ar:فِي}} ({{tr:fī}}) makes the earth the domain within which the subjected things are located. Its containment force can include interior and surface-location shades, but here it chiefly defines the earth-field of benefit.

topics.headline: earth as containment domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the first benefit-field as an earth-contained domain rather than an unbounded list.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the following definite earth noun and gives the relative object its domain.

words.gloss_range: the known lower earth-domain, first as benefit-containing field
words.root_gloss_range: ground, land, earth, and lower realm; local use is the definite lower domain under the sky
words.prose: The first {{ar:ٱلْأَرْضِ}} ({{tr:al-arḍi}}) names the known lower domain as the field of subjection and benefit. Because the same noun returns later as an impact target, this first occurrence prepares a shift from earth as useful domain to earth as threatened surface.

topics.headline: earth as benefit field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the earth first as the familiar lower realm filled with things made serviceable.
topics.reason: The definite noun is governed by the locative preposition and denotes the known earth-domain.

topics.headline: earth-sky vertical axis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah builds a vertical axis: the earth named here will reappear beneath the restrained sky.
topics.reason: The rows track the repeated earth noun and its relation to the sky term later in the verse.

words.gloss_range: bound conjunction adding the ship scene to the subjected object field while allowing a clause pivot
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) joins the ship scene to the earth-domain, extending the field of subjection from land to sea. Its position also creates a pivot where the ship can be heard as coordinated object and as the front of the following motion scene.

topics.headline: ship coordination pivot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the catalogue expanding by coordination while the ship word also prepares the following motion clause.
topics.reason: The conjunction attaches the ship noun to the prior object field and stands at the boundary of the ship-motion unit.

words.gloss_range: the familiar vessel-class, locally under subjection and immediately described as moving at sea
words.root_gloss_range: ship and orbit/falak resonance; local noun selects vessel sense, with orbit resonance secondary
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْفُلْكَ}} ({{tr:al-fulka}}) brings the familiar vessel-class into the subjected field and immediately into the sea-motion scene. The root resonance with orbit remains a useful background, but the local noun and surrounding sea verb select ships, with the case and variant evidence showing how tightly this word pivots between object and moving sign; the ship-sea-coursing cluster is also a familiar sign cluster at 2:164.

topics.headline: vessel-class under subjection
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices ships as a familiar class made serviceable, not a single incidental boat.
topics.reason: The noun is definite and functions in the object field, while its form can serve singular or plural vessel sense.

topics.headline: ship sense with orbit resonance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a wider circular-motion resonance in the root family, while the local sea setting keeps vessels as the selected sense.
topics.reason: The root can connect ship and orbit fields, but the surrounding sea and motion words select the vessel branch locally.

topics.headline: case pivot in sign cluster
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ship word as a pivot between subjugated object and moving sign, with the familiar ship-sea-coursing cluster also found at 2:164.
topics.reason: The supplied rows preserve both the canonical accusative role and variant/collocational pressure without displacing the local vessel reading.

words.gloss_range: ongoing coursing of ships, with water-flow and ordered-motion associations
words.root_gloss_range: running, flowing, coursing, ship movement, celestial movement, and event-course; local use is ship motion in the sea
words.prose: {{ar:تَجْرِي}} ({{tr:tajrī}}) turns the ship into an ongoing motion scene, using feminine singular agreement with the vessel noun and indicative force. The root's running and flowing range supports ship-coursing here, and same-surah river-motion echoes at 22:14 and 22:23 make the motion feel part of a wider blessed-flow register.

topics.headline: ongoing ship-coursing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ship not only as subjected object but as actively coursing in an ongoing scene.
topics.reason: The imperfect indicative verb agrees with the ship noun and supplies the motion clause.

topics.headline: flow range in vessel motion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices ship movement as a form of coursing within a broader flow vocabulary, with same-surah river echoes at 22:14 and 22:23.
topics.reason: The root range includes water, ships, and cosmic motion, but the local subject and sea phrase select vessel-coursing.

words.gloss_range: locative medium marker for ship traversal in or through the sea
words.prose: {{ar:فِي}} ({{tr:fī}}) makes the sea the medium of traversal. The ships do not merely exist beside the sea; their coursing takes place in, through, or across it.

topics.headline: sea as traversal medium
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the sea as the medium through which the subjected ships move.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the sea noun and marks the setting of the ship-motion clause.

words.gloss_range: the known vast sea as the medium of ship motion
words.root_gloss_range: sea, vastness, expanse, and split-open depth; local use is the definite sea medium
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْبَحْرِ}} ({{tr:al-baḥri}}) names the known vast medium through which the ships course. Its breadth and depth associations matter because the ayah presents not only vessels but vessels moving through a dangerous expanse under divine command, as part of the recurring ship-sea sign cluster rather than scenery alone.

topics.headline: vast sea medium
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ship sign as movement through a vast and deep medium, not simple travel over neutral space.
topics.reason: The definite sea noun is locally the motion medium, with supplied lexical rows preserving breadth and depth associations.

topics.headline: ship-sea sign cluster
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the sea term as part of the recurring ship-sea sign cluster rather than as scenery alone.
topics.reason: The rows connect the sea noun with divine-name, ship, and motion fields.

words.gloss_range: instrumental or causal preposition attaching ship motion to divine command
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) attaches the ship motion to divine command as instrument or cause. The preposition prevents the sea scene from reading as autonomous natural motion; it marks the motion as governed.

topics.headline: motion by command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ships' coursing is explicitly tied to divine command, not left as a self-contained process.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the command noun and attaches that phrase to the ship-motion scene.

words.gloss_range: his command or governing affair as the operative principle behind ship motion
words.root_gloss_range: command, order, affair, matter, and authoritative decree; local use centers command as governing cause
words.prose: {{ar:أَمْرِهِۦ}} ({{tr:amrihi}}) nominalizes command as the operative principle by which the ships course. The suffix keeps that command personally tied to God, and the term later pairs with permission, so the ayah distinguishes governance that enables motion from permission that conditions possible collapse.

topics.headline: owned governing command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices command as a named governing principle owned by God, not merely an implied cause.
topics.reason: The noun is genitive under the preceding preposition and definite by a third-person suffix.

topics.headline: command-affair range narrowed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that command carries an affair/order range, while the local ship-motion phrase makes authoritative command the active center.
topics.reason: The broader semantic range is preserved, but the instrumental phrase with ship motion selects command as governing cause.

topics.headline: command and permission pair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices two authority terms bracketing two domains: command for sea-motion and permission for sky-fall.
topics.reason: The rows connect this command phrase with the later permission phrase as a paired governance structure.

words.gloss_range: conjunction shifting from enabled provision to restrained harm without repeating the subject
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) adds the sky-restraint clause without renaming the subject. The conjunction marks a new beat: from provision and movement to the prevention of harm.

topics.headline: shift to restraint beat
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the catalogue pivoting from what is made available to what is held back.
topics.reason: The conjunction coordinates a second divine-act clause while the subject remains recoverable from the prior clause.

words.gloss_range: ongoing active restraint or withholding of the sky from falling
words.root_gloss_range: grip, hold, retain, withhold, restrain; local Form IV selects active restraint
words.prose: {{ar:يُمْسِكُ}} ({{tr:yumsiku}}) changes the ayah from completed subjection to ongoing restraint. The Form IV grip-and-withholding sense makes the sky's stability an active divine holding, with the prevented falling clause naming what that restraint averts; the parallel at 35:41 reinforces the sky-holding motif, and the clipped consonant cluster gives the phrase a holding texture.

topics.headline: ongoing restraint after completed subjection
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah shift from a completed act of making serviceable to a continuing act of holding back danger.
topics.reason: The imperfect verb contrasts with the earlier perfect verb and heads the second divine-action unit.

topics.headline: active withholding grip
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices stability as restraint from a named collapse, not as passive stillness.
topics.reason: The verb governs the sky object and a prevented-event complement, while Form IV sharpens the hold/withhold field.

topics.headline: sky-holding parallel and sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the sky-restraint expression as a recognizable motif, with the clipped consonant cluster adding a holding texture.
topics.reason: The rows cite the parallel at 35:41 and preserve the phonetic observation as a local sound payoff.

words.gloss_range: the definite upper sky or canopy as the object being held back from collapse
words.root_gloss_range: height, sky, upper surface, canopy, with a secondary marking/name dispute; local use is the upper sky
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلسَّمَآءَ}} ({{tr:as-samāʾa}}) is the direct object of restraint: the upper canopy is being held. Its height and canopy range is locally active, while derivational alternatives remain secondary; the word begins the final cosmic segment by turning from enabled benefit to prevented harm over the earth.

topics.headline: held upper canopy
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the sky as the held object, the upper canopy whose fall is being prevented.
topics.reason: The noun is accusative as the object of the restraint verb and denotes the definite upper sky.

topics.headline: height branch selected
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the sky term carrying height and canopy pressure, while the marking/name dispute does not redirect the local sense.
topics.reason: The local syntax and collapse clause select the sky/height branch, not an alternative marking sense.

topics.headline: sky over earth collapse axis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the sky-earth relation turning into a threatened collapse axis after the land and sea benefit scenes.
topics.reason: The rows place the sky between the holding verb and the falling complement and connect it to the earth target and to 35:41.

words.gloss_range: subjunctive particle turning falling into the prevented event within the restraint clause
words.prose: {{ar:أَنْ}} ({{tr:an}}) turns the fall into a governed event: what is being held back is that the sky should fall on the earth. Its infinitival and prevention force lets the restraint clause name the danger from inside the syntax.

topics.headline: prevented falling event
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah names the averted catastrophe directly rather than simply saying the sky is held.
topics.reason: The particle governs the following subjunctive verb and forms the prevented-event complement of the restraint verb.

words.gloss_range: subjunctive falling or occurrence of the sky-collapse event
words.prose: {{ar:تَقَعَ}} ({{tr:taqaʿa}}) gives the restrained danger an event-word: the sky would fall and the fall would occur. The Form I and subjunctive frame keep the action as falling, not caused infliction, while the wider collapse motif recalls 52:44 and 34:9.

topics.headline: subjunctive fall event
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the danger expressed as an actual fall-event held in subjunctive dependence.
topics.reason: The verb is subjunctive under the preceding particle and remains Form I falling rather than causative action.

topics.headline: physical fall with event force
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the fall is also an occurrence, making collapse feel like an event that is being prevented.
topics.reason: The root range includes falling and occurrence; the local sky-earth construction selects physical fall while retaining event pressure.

topics.headline: celestial collapse motif
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the prevented sky-fall as part of a wider celestial-collapse motif, including 52:44 and 34:9.
topics.reason: The rows cite explicit cross-references for the sky-fall motif.

words.gloss_range: directional and contact preposition marking the earth as impact surface
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَى}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) makes the earth the surface under the threatened fall. Its contact and pressure force turns the sky-earth relation into impact, and the assimilation variant exposes how tightly the preposition and earth noun can sound together.

topics.headline: earth as impact surface
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the danger is not only descent but impact upon the earth.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the following earth noun and marks the target surface of the potential fall.

topics.headline: preposition-noun fusion variant
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a recitational pressure point where the impact phrase can be audibly fused.
topics.reason: The qirāʾa row is useful as form evidence for phrase cohesion without changing the canonical local syntax.

words.gloss_range: the same definite earth now as lower surface beneath possible sky-fall
words.root_gloss_range: ground, land, earth, and lower realm; local use is the ground/lower realm as impact target
words.prose: The second {{ar:ٱلْأَرْضِ}} ({{tr:al-arḍi}}) is the same definite earth, but now under a different governor and role. What was first the field of benefit becomes the surface of possible catastrophe, making the ayah's mercy depend on both provision and restraint.

topics.headline: earth as impact target
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices earth as the lower realm beneath the threatened sky-fall, not merely the source of benefits.
topics.reason: The noun is governed by the preceding preposition and functions as the target of the potential fall.

topics.headline: same earth, changed role
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the repeated definite earth shifting from provision-domain to catastrophe-zone while preserving the same referent.
topics.reason: The repeated definite noun is governed first by a locative and then by an impact preposition, with a sound variant reinforcing phrase cohesion.

words.gloss_range: exception particle restricting sky-fall to divine permission
words.prose: {{ar:إِلَّا}} ({{tr:illā}}) pivots the fall from impossible under present restraint to possible only under permission. The exception makes collapse contingent rather than autonomous.

topics.headline: collapse restricted to permission
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the sky's fall is not denied as unthinkable; it is made contingent on divine permission alone.
topics.reason: The exception particle follows an implied negative restraint and introduces the sole condition for the prevented event.

words.gloss_range: causal or instrumental preposition making permission the condition within the exception
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) makes permission the causal condition inside the exception. It also echoes the earlier command phrase, aligning ship-motion by command with sky-fall only by permission.

topics.headline: permission as causal condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices permission functioning as the condition that alone could allow the prevented fall.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the permission noun within the exception phrase.

topics.headline: command-permission preposition echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the repeated preposition aligning the two governance phrases in the ayah.
topics.reason: The row explicitly links the command phrase and the permission phrase through repeated prepositional structure.

words.gloss_range: his permission as the personalized condition for any sky-fall
words.root_gloss_range: ear, hearing, listening, permission, announcement, authorization; local use selects permission/authorization
words.prose: {{ar:إِذْنِهِۦٓ}} ({{tr:idhnihi}}) names permission as God's own authorization, the only condition under which the sky could fall. The root's hearing and announcement field remains background to authorization, while the formula at 2:97, 2:249, and 3:49 and same-surah echoes at 22:27, 22:39, and 22:46 tie permission to proclaimed and authorized acts; here it answers the earlier command term as the second control word.

topics.headline: owned permission condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the condition for collapse as personalized divine permission, not an impersonal law.
topics.reason: The noun is genitive after the preposition and definite by the third-person suffix.

topics.headline: authorization branch selected
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices permission as part of a hearing-announcement-authorization root field, while local syntax selects authorization.
topics.reason: The root range is broader, but the exception phrase requires permission or authorization as the local sense.

topics.headline: permission formula and boundary echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the phrase as a formula for conditioned extraordinary events and as the answer to the earlier command phrase.
topics.reason: The rows cite formulaic examples at 2:97, 2:249, and 3:49, same-surah echoes at 22:27, 22:39, and 22:46, and the command-permission pairing.

words.gloss_range: emphatic particle opening the nominal compassion conclusion
words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:inna}}) opens the closing nominal clause with emphasis. After the earth, sea, and sky examples, the particle turns the catalogue into an asserted conclusion about divine compassion toward people.

topics.headline: emphatic compassion conclusion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final attributes as the asserted interpretation of the preceding cosmic signs.
topics.reason: The particle opens a nominal clause, governs the following divine name, and combines with the later emphatic lām.

words.gloss_range: repeated proper divine name as subject of the final compassion predication
words.root_gloss_range: proper divine-name field; local use is the repeated named subject of the nominal clause
words.prose: The second {{ar:ٱللَّهَ}} ({{tr:allāha}}) restarts the final clause with the explicit divine name instead of a pronoun. That repetition links the agent of subjection and restraint with the one now predicated as tender and merciful toward people.

topics.headline: repeated name as attribute subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah deliberately repeating the divine name to connect cosmic agency with the final compassion predicates.
topics.reason: The repeated proper name is the accusative subject of the emphatic nominal clause and receives the compassion predicates.

words.gloss_range: preposition directing the compassion predicates toward people and echoing earlier governance phrases
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) directs the closing attributes toward humanity, making people the specified concern of compassion. Its fronted phrase stands between the divine name and the predicates, and it echoes the earlier command and permission phrases so that governance language resolves into human-directed mercy.

topics.headline: human-directed compassion relation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the attributes are not abstract; their relation is directed toward people.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the people noun and the phrase is fronted before the compassion predicates.

topics.headline: preposition echo resolves in mercy
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the repeated preposition carrying the ayah from command, to permission, to the human object of compassion, with local resonance after 22:2 and 22:18.
topics.reason: The rows explicitly compare this phrase with the earlier command and permission phrases and with the surah's address to people at 22:2 and 22:18.

words.gloss_range: the definite human collective as the object of compassion
words.root_gloss_range: people, humankind, social ease and intimacy, with a debated forgetfulness derivation; local use is humanity collectively
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلنَّاسِ}} ({{tr:an-nāsi}}) universalizes the closing object from the immediate plural addressees to humanity as a definite collective. The sociability and vulnerability debates sharpen the human need for compassion, and the word's position places people between the divine name and the mercy attributes.

topics.headline: human collective and derivation pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the mercy object as humanity collectively, with social need and vulnerability adding pressure without replacing the local collective sense.
topics.reason: The definite noun denotes people or humankind; derivational disputes remain meaningful but do not displace the local collective reference.

topics.headline: people enclosed in predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices humanity grammatically positioned between the divine name and the compassion predicates.
topics.reason: The rows connect the people noun with the divine name and mercy roots and point to its placement inside the final predicate structure.

words.gloss_range: emphatic lām attached to the first compassion predicate
words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) places the second layer of emphasis directly on the first compassion predicate. The closing mercy claim is therefore formally asserted, not softly appended after the cosmic catalogue.

topics.headline: emphasis fused to predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the compassion predicate receiving its own visible emphatic mark after the earlier emphatic opener.
topics.reason: The emphatic lām is attached to the predicate in the construction opened by the earlier emphatic particle.

words.gloss_range: first compassion predicate, intensive tender solicitude especially as preventive tenderness
words.root_gloss_range: raʾfa as tender compassion, solicitude, and preventive kindness; local adjective is an intensive predicate
words.prose: {{ar:رَءُوفٌ}} ({{tr:raʾūfun}}) is the first predicate of the closing clause, making tenderness a predicated divine quality. Its preventive compassion comes before {{ar:رَحِيمٌ}} ({{tr:raḥīmun}}), and the intensive pattern, tanwīn, variant length, and tight pairing with mercy make the tenderness durable and marked.

topics.headline: first compassion predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices tenderness stated as a predicate of God, not as another narrated action.
topics.reason: The adjective is nominative as the first predicate in the emphatic nominal clause and is indefinite with tanwīn.

topics.headline: preventive tenderness before mercy
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the closing sequence beginning with tenderness that prevents harm before broader mercy is named.
topics.reason: The supplied semantics distinguish this tenderness from the following broader mercy and make the order meaningful.

topics.headline: intensive marked pair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the attribute as morphologically intensive and distributionally marked within a tight compassion pair.
topics.reason: The rows preserve the intensive pattern, long-vowel variant contrast, rarity of the root, and frequent pairing with the mercy root.

words.gloss_range: second compassion predicate sealing the ayah with durable encompassing mercy
words.root_gloss_range: mercy, womb-related nurture, compassion, and seeking mercy; local adjective is an intensive divine predicate
words.prose: {{ar:رَحِيمٌ}} ({{tr:raḥīmun}}) completes the predicate pair and seals the ayah on durable mercy. The root's womb-mercy field makes the final word an image of enveloping care, while the formula with {{ar:رَءُوفٌ}} ({{tr:raʾūfun}}), known from 2:143 and 9:128, interprets earth-service, sea-motion, and sky-restraint as compassion toward people. The shared final cadence then softens the close after the hard sky-fall image.

topics.headline: second mercy predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah ending not with another act but with a durable mercy predicate completing the nominal seal.
topics.reason: The adjective is the second nominative predicate and shares the indefinite attribute form of the preceding predicate.

topics.headline: mercy system and womb image
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices mercy as a larger lexical system with intimate nurture imagery, while local grammar keeps the adjective predicate as the selected form.
topics.reason: The broader derivative family and womb association enrich the predicate but do not replace the local adjective function.

topics.headline: recognized compassion formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final word completing a recognized compassion pair also associated with 2:143 and 9:128.
topics.reason: The rows identify the paired intensive attributes and cite explicit formula parallels.

topics.headline: cosmic catalogue sealed as mercy
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final mercy word interpreting the whole earth-sea-sky catalogue as care directed toward people.
topics.reason: The rows track the movement from 22:64 possession, through concrete domains, to the final human-directed compassion seal.

topics.headline: soft final cadence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final paired cadence softening the close after the hard image of sky-fall.
topics.reason: The sound rows identify the shared final cadence and acoustic resolution of the closing pair.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The opening appeal to see, followed by subjection, vessel-motion, sea, and command.
baseline_models.mechanism: Reflective perception follows a causal chain: terrestrial things are made serviceable, a vessel is carried through a wide medium, and its actual motion remains governed rather than self-originating.

activation_trace.role: Seeing by reflective judgment turns the opening into an invitation to infer an ordering cause.
The split target's deliberative sense reinforces considered seeing rather than bare eyesight.
Purpose-directed subjection supplies the relation by which the environment becomes usable.
The water-going vessel is the concrete body whose serviceability is tested in motion.
Actual running and streaming provide the enabled movement in the mechanism.
The abundant wide water supplies the resistant medium through which directed motion occurs.
Command supplies the governing direction that converts possible motion into ordered passage.

changed_reading.before: A list of useful natural objects offered to people.
changed_reading.after: An observable chain of directed affordance in which access, conveyance, medium, and motion remain dependent on command.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The ship is allowed to run horizontally while the sky is prevented from falling vertically upon the doubled earth.
baseline_models.mechanism: The ayah couples two opposite controls of motion: useful transit is released and catastrophic descent is restrained. Earth below, sky above, flow, holding, fall, and permission form one actively regulated spatial system.

activation_trace.role: The lower surface occurs on both the serviceable and threatened sides of the spatial mechanism.
Rotation and circular movement make the vessel part of a kinetic rather than static cosmos.
Holding and confining supply the active brake on destructive movement.
What is elevated and overarches the earth supplies the restrained upper body.
Falling and becoming fixed at a destination supply the blocked downward trajectory.
Permission makes restraint selective rather than an absolute denial that any descent can occur.

changed_reading.before: Two independent wonders, navigation and a stable sky.
changed_reading.after: One asymmetric motion-control system that releases beneficial movement while withholding ruinous movement.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The operational clauses culminate in tenderness and mercy directed to people.
baseline_models.mechanism: The final attributes causally recolor what precedes them: making passage possible and preventing collapse are not demonstrations detached from human life but the production of a familiar, non-desolate habitat.

activation_trace.role: Facilitated service supplies the positive, enabling side of habitable mercy.
Protective holding supplies mercy's preventive side.
Human familiarity that removes desolation makes inhabitation, not abstraction, the beneficiary.
Tender compassion explicitly names the protective motive of the system.
Merciful care binds enabling and prevention into one human-directed function.

changed_reading.before: Compassion is a devotional epilogue after a display of power.
changed_reading.after: Compassion is the interpretive key: power is shown as habitat-making service and continuous protection.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah's shaking, plunge from the sky, wind-driven descent, and threatened demolition turn divine holding into active inhibition of cascading collapse across several scales.

activation_trace.role: Active holding remains the focus mechanism that counters collapse.
The severe descending event gives the withheld fall catastrophic force.
Opening disturbance supplies the surah-wide possibility that stable ground can convulse.
A noisy uncontrolled fall from the sky gives a human-scale image of lost support.
Plunging into an abyss extends falling into irreversible displacement.
Building collapse supplies the social and architectural scale of what restraint preserves.

structural_cues: The surah opens with earth-shaking before the focus ayah presents held sky over doubled earth.
The sky-fall simile at 22:31 and counterfactual demolition at 22:40 make collapse a repeated mechanism, not a stray image.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies shaking, uncontrolled descent, demolition, and focus holding; I treat them as scale-varied instances of a collapse/counter-collapse pattern. They may alternatively be separate rhetorical warnings that only intensify the focus clause's stakes.

changed_reading.before: The sky's non-fall is a static fact of nature.
changed_reading.after: Non-fall is ongoing merciful work that inhibits cascading cosmic, bodily, and built collapse.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately preceding descent of water and greening of earth activates the focus root's rainfall branch: the sky is held from catastrophic fall while authorized descent is released as life-giving rain.

activation_trace.role: Rainfall is a literal branch of falling, allowing a beneficial reading of authorized descent.
A holding place for water turns restraint into storage before release.
Authorization distinguishes permitted precipitation from indiscriminate collapse.
Delivered descent supplies the controlled downward movement immediately before the focus.
Water conveyed by pouring specifies what beneficial descent carries.
Fresh vegetation supplies the life-producing result of selective release.

structural_cues: 22:63 places sky-water-earth-greening only two ayat before sky-holding and earth-impact.
The focus exception follows the verb of falling rather than merely restating divine power.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies immediate rain descent, a rainfall branch for the focus verb, water retention, and an authorization exception; I infer a controlled storage/release contrast. The live alternative is that the exception refers only to a future catastrophic fall.

changed_reading.before: Except by permission merely reserves God's ability to cause the feared catastrophe.
changed_reading.after: Permission can also discriminate destructive mass-fall from the measured falling that waters and greens the earth.

context_deltas.mechanism: Reciprocal entry of night and day, followed by water entering the terrestrial system, reframes the focus cosmos as selectively permeable: useful crossings and currents are enabled while boundary-destroying collapse is checked.

activation_trace.role: Mutual entry supplies a model of boundaries that admit transition without disappearing.
Night supplies one phase that repeatedly crosses into and out of its counterpart.
Flow supplies an admitted horizontal crossing through the sea.
Holding supplies the complementary limit that keeps permeability from becoming collapse.

structural_cues: The sequence 22:61-65 moves through reciprocal temporal entry, water descent, possession of both realms, maritime passage, and restrained vertical fall.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated crossings and one explicit restraint; I infer a shared rule of managed permeability. The alternative is a looser catalogue of signs with no single boundary mechanism.

changed_reading.before: Earth, sea, and sky are fixed stacked regions kept in place.
changed_reading.after: They form a dynamic system whose boundaries admit ordered passage, phase change, and rain while refusing indiscriminate collapse.

context_deltas.mechanism: The same subjection verb applied to sacrificial animals is directed toward gratitude and piety rather than material transfer to God. That repeated pattern makes terrestrial service an entrusted benefit with a required human response.

activation_trace.role: Purpose-directed service in the focus supplies the benefit whose ethical direction is at issue.
The repeated verb ties usable animal service directly to a ritual discipline.
Recognition of benefit names the intended response to what has been made serviceable.
The reach relation separates consumed matter from the inward quality that matters.
Self-protective piety supplies the ethical interior that should answer material benefit.
The second repetition confirms that subjection is framed by guidance and response, not possession alone.

structural_cues: 22:36-37 repeatedly joins serviceability to eating, sharing, gratitude, piety, guidance, and doing good.
The focus retains the beneficiary phrase for you, allowing that earlier ethical frame to travel forward.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the same verb and an explicit gratitude/piety frame; I carry that frame into the focus as an ethical entailment of benefit. The alternative is that the ritual case governs sacrifice only and does not constrain every use of earth and sea.

changed_reading.before: What is subjected is simply available for human use.
changed_reading.after: Serviceability is a trust whose proper return is gratitude, restraint, and shared benefit rather than bare entitlement.

context_deltas.mechanism: Divine defense and the checking of some people by others to prevent demolition activate holding as counter-pressure. Preservation may work through balanced opposing forces rather than only through motionless suspension.

activation_trace.role: Holding supplies the focus's preservation against a threatening trajectory.
Repelling harm supplies an explicit divine counterforce at the social scale.
One human force checking another makes preservation mediated and dynamic.
The averted collapse of buildings specifies what balanced checking preserves.

structural_cues: 22:38-40 moves from divine defense to plural human counteraction and then to preserved worship spaces.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repulsion, mediated checking, and averted demolition; I map their counterforce structure onto sky-holding. The live alternative is a moral analogy only, not an account of how cosmic restraint operates.

changed_reading.before: Holding means unilateral static support from above.
changed_reading.after: Holding can mean active balancing in which destructive force is checked through another force so a plural habitat survives.

context_deltas.mechanism: Travel through earth, reasoning hearts, and the contrast between ocular and inward blindness turn the focus's seeing into disciplined inference. The perceiver must cognitively restrain error while reading a world physically held from collapse.

activation_trace.role: Reflective seeing anchors the focus as an act of judgment.
Travel and movement make terrestrial observation an active inquiry rather than passive spectacle.
Reason as a restraint against ignorance supplies the perceiver's own holding function.
Blindness of inward perception identifies the failure that the focus question challenges.
Heart-insight distinguishes causal recognition from merely seeing visible surfaces.

structural_cues: 22:46 explicitly relocates blindness from eyes to hearts after commanding movement through earth.
The repeated opening formula at 22:63 and 22:65 asks the reader to infer from processes rather than inspect isolated objects.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies travel, heart-reason, inward blindness, and the focus appeal to see; I infer that the sign requires disciplined causal reading. The alternative is that the opening remains a conventional attention marker without a distinct epistemic demand.

changed_reading.before: See means notice an impressive visible arrangement.
changed_reading.after: See means reason through enabled motion and withheld collapse with a heart capable of restraining error.

context_deltas.mechanism: Permission for resistance, dispute over command, and the denial of authority to rival objects turn command and permission into an authorization architecture. Effective routing and restraint display legitimate power, while unsupported claims fail that test.

activation_trace.role: Binding direction supplies the focus operation's normative source.
Permission supplies explicit authorization for an otherwise restrained event.
Authorized resistance gives permission a legal and protective use elsewhere in the surah.
The disputed command makes order a contested claim requiring rightful direction.
Power and delegated authority supply the criterion explicitly absent from rival worship.

structural_cues: The latter surah repeats permission, command, judgment, knowledge, and authority across legal and cultic disputes.
The focus uniquely shows command and permission accomplishing both movement and restraint.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies legal permission, contested command, absent rival authority, and effective focus operations; I infer efficacy plus authorization as a test of legitimate rule. The alternative is that physical command and legal-cultic authority should remain separate domains.

changed_reading.before: By His command and permission are formulas of sheer fiat.
changed_reading.after: They mark a legible authorization order whose legitimacy is displayed in beneficial efficacy and protective restraint.

context_deltas.mechanism: The fly parable tests rival capacity by creation and retrieval. Against that failure, the focus's successful service, routing, and restraint become operational evidence, while people remain dependent beneficiaries rather than controllers.

activation_trace.role: Successful direction toward human use supplies positive operational capacity.
Successful protective restraint supplies the complementary capacity.
Creating a living thing establishes the first explicit capacity test.
Failure to extract something from another's grasp establishes a second test of control.
Lack of strength names the shared incapacity of seeker and sought.
The pursuit relation exposes dependence on what neither side can secure.

structural_cues: 22:73 contrasts invoked rivals' inability with the focus's already demonstrated creation-order and control.
22:74 immediately says divine power has not been properly measured.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies explicit creation/retrieval failure and successful focus operations; I infer a comparative capacity test. The alternative is that the fly parable targets idols only without revising how human benefit in the focus should be understood.

changed_reading.before: The ayah is a reassuring catalogue of benefits under human reach.
changed_reading.after: It is also a humility test: humans receive a functioning order whose creation, routing, and preservation they do not control.

context_deltas.mechanism: The final imperative to hold fast to God echoes the focus predicate by which God holds the sky. Cosmic preservation becomes a relational invitation: the held creature responds by attaching itself to the Holder.

activation_trace.role: Divine holding supplies the prior act of prevention and preservation.
Holding that prevents and preserves becomes the human imperative at the surah's close.

structural_cues: The surah closes by naming God as patron and helper immediately after commanding attachment to Him.
The focus has already rendered divine preservation as an act of holding.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two distinct roots with the same preserve-by-holding mechanism; I infer a responsive relation from God's cosmic act to human attachment. The alternative is a poetic echo without a deliberate reciprocal structure.

changed_reading.before: God holds the sky while humans merely observe the fact.
changed_reading.after: The cosmic holding anticipates a human response: hold fast to the One whose prior holding makes life possible.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This bodily-to-cosmic analogy is surprising, but the focus itself joins a womb-holding branch of holding to mercy, while 22:5 supplies retention in wombs. It should be rendered as a habitat analogy about protected development, never as a claim that the sky is literally a womb.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus words for holding and mercy can both activate uterine containment around the earth below.

activation_trace.role: The womb-holding branch makes protective retention materially bodily rather than abstract.
The womb sense inside mercy supplies an enclosure in which vulnerable life develops.
Retention and stable settlement supply the temporal protection required for development.
The explicit developmental container elsewhere in the surah grounds the analogy.

changed_reading.before: The world is protected externally by a ceiling held up.
changed_reading.after: The earth-sky relation can also be imagined as a merciful enclosure that retains fragile life until it can grow.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The sky-to-marking target is form-distant and therefore surprising, yet its first-rain image is anchored in the focus sky and locally corroborated by 22:63's water and greening. Downstream prose should identify it as a split-root activation, not replace the ordinary meaning of sky with mark.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus sky's non-dominant mapped target and the focus rainfall branch converge on earth marked by permitted rain.

activation_trace.role: The supplied split target's first rain marks earth with vegetation, making sky active in producing a visible trace.
Rainfall gives the marking event a focus-internal mode of descent.
Delivered descent supplies the nearby activation that brings the split image alive.
Green growth is the visible mark left on earth.

changed_reading.before: The sky is only a passive upper body prevented from falling.
changed_reading.after: In a contained split-root reading, the sky also marks earth through the first permitted rain that leaves it green.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The compelled-unpaid-labor branch makes the language of service ethically uneasy, but repeated subjection in 22:36-37 is bounded by gratitude and piety. Render this as a caution against extractive entitlement, not as a claim that the focus lexeme denotes slavery in context.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus's subjection of what is on earth for people contains an available coercive-labor shadow.

activation_trace.role: Compelled labor without compensation exposes the exploitative possibility inside human use.
The repeated service relation provides the ritual case that disciplines the shadow.
Grateful recognition redirects use away from self-authorizing possession.
Pious self-guarding supplies an internal check on extractive appetite.

changed_reading.before: For you grants an uncomplicated right of use.
changed_reading.after: For you can carry a moral burden: service received without gratitude and restraint risks reproducing the coercive shadow of serviceability.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is a cross-domain transfer from cosmic mechanics to revelation. It remains anchored through the focus branches of holding and written impact and through 22:52's removal and firming, but prose must present it only as an analogy for selective stabilization, not as the physical referent of the focus clause.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Holding prevents a fall in the focus, while a writing-related branch of falling permits an analogy to material inserted into and stabilized within a text.

activation_trace.role: Holding supplies the selective stabilization that keeps an order from collapsing.
The writing-impact branch supplies the narrow lexical bridge from falling to inscription.
Removal followed by replacement supplies the filtering operation.
Making firm and exact supplies the stabilized result after disruptive insertion.

changed_reading.before: Holding applies only to physical mass above earth.
changed_reading.after: As a contained analogy, the same hold/filter pattern can illuminate how disruptive insertion is removed while signs are made firm.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The agent-or-messenger branch of running is not the ordinary sense of the ship's motion, so this reading is intentionally branch-distant. Selection of messengers and return of affairs keep it traceable, but it should appear only as a commissioned-conveyance analogy alongside the literal vessel reading.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus joins the running vessel to command, allowing a minor branch in which the runner is an agent or messenger.

activation_trace.role: An agent or messenger carried under direction supplies commissioned conveyance inside the focus motion.
Command supplies the commission that directs the carrier.
Selection supplies the commissioning step for designated carriers.
Messenger and message make the conveyed agency explicit in the later context.
Return supplies the completion of a dispatched route back to its source.
Affairs as matters returning to God close the command-and-return circuit.

changed_reading.before: The ship is only cargo-bearing transport through water.
changed_reading.after: In an exploratory parallel, its commanded running images commissioned conveyance: selected carriers move an entrusted matter and the route returns to its source.

strongest_changes: The held sky and the authorized exception can coexist as selective storage and release: destructive fall is checked while rain is permitted to green earth.
Repeated subjection in the ritual section redirects human benefit from entitlement toward gratitude, piety, and trust.
Shaking, falling, demolition, and social counterforce turn holding from static support into active prevention and balancing.
The final command to hold fast converts observed cosmic preservation into a responsive human relation to the Holder.
summary.what_was_special: The ayah sustained several coexisting readings because its mechanism is asymmetrical: it enables current, restrains collapse, and permits selected descent. Immediate rain context, repeated service language, legal authorization, perceptual discipline, and non-dominant mapped branches activated ecological, ethical, social, epistemic, uterine, textual, and messenger-like readings without displacing the literal maritime and cosmic scene.
remaining_uncertainties: The permission exception may reserve only catastrophic sky-fall rather than also naming beneficial rain release.
The social counterforce and authorization readings may be analogical echoes rather than mechanisms intended to govern the cosmic clause.
The first-rain marker, womb-world, textual-hold, and messenger-current readings depend on form-distant or cross-domain branches and must remain explicitly contained.
The ethical limit on terrestrial use is strongly activated by repeated subjection but is inferred rather than directly legislated in the focus ayah.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Human mobility depends on commanded flows and held boundaries.** `س خ ر B001` subjects for a purpose; `ف ل ك B003/B001` ship and turning roundness; `ج ر ي B001` flow; `ب ح ر B001/B002` broad abundant water; `م س ك B001/B004` holding restraint and firm water-holding place; `و ق ع B001/B002` falling into hard occurrence. The ship moves while the sky is held. I infer that usable mobility requires some elements released into flow and others restrained from collapse. The world reads as a differentiated support system, not uniformly passive matter.
2. **Permission marks the limit between preservation and event.** `ء ذ ن B004` authorization and `ء م ر B002` directive distinguish ordinary holding from exceptional falling. I infer that catastrophe is not autonomous breakdown but remains within a permission boundary. `ر ء ف B001` tender compassion and `ر ح م B001` mercy assign the system's ongoing restraint a protective role toward people.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 22:73 corrected any passive reading of subjected creation: a tiny fly can strip the supposed powers and defeat their collective attempt at recovery.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **A navigable world is maintained by enabling one motion and restraining another.** Fixed `سَخَّر` activates `س خ ر:B001` (bringing under command for a purpose), `ٱلْفُلْك` activates `ف ل ك:B003` (ship), `تَجْرِى` uses `ج ر ي:B001`, and `ٱلْبَحْر` uses `ب ح ر:B001` (wide abundant water). In parallel, `يُمْسِك` activates `م س ك:B001` (holding and restraining), and potential sky-fall activates `و ق ع:B001` (falling into occurrence) with `B002` (hard descent), allowed only by `ء ذ ن:B004` (permission). `22:63` supplied beneficial descent; here uncontrolled descent is withheld. The packet supplies command-enabled flow and permission-bounded fall; I infer that habitability lies in their regulated middle. Compassion is environmental governance, not only episodic rescue.
2. **Mercy holds a potentially oscillating human field.** Fixed `ٱلنَّاس` permits `ن و س:B001` (swaying oscillation), while `رَءُوف` activates `ر ء ف:B001` and `رَّحِيم` activates `ر ح م:B001`. The maintained ground-sky interval gives unstable humanity room to move without cosmic collapse. I infer that tenderness here acts structurally by preserving that interval.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: `22:66` brings the environmental preservation inward as life, death, and revived life. The later sequence makes the fixed mercy a condition of continued human existence, not only protection from falling sky.
